advances: Global evenness in the shifted-mass theorem `f0ff12aa81c7461c` cannot be replaced by coordinate-sign symmetry and mean zero of the complete original lattice table. The full shifted-mass ratio is unbounded already in fixed integer dimension two, after optimizing over every central cutoff. The identical example also has an unbounded single-parity ratio. This concerns the proposed extension of the shifted-mass comparison; it makes no assertion of failure for the original hitting score, actual mixed-integer halfspace depth, or the locked weak Oertel conjecture.

proof:
The box \(Q_h\) is compact, convex, invariant under both coordinate sign changes, and contains the nonempty open rectangle \((-h,h)\times(-1,1)\). The maximum in the definition of \(F_h\) is also the maximum of the five affine functions \(0\), \(x-2hy\), \(-x-2hy\), \(x+8hy-6h\), and \(-x+8hy-6h\). It is therefore finite and convex on all of \(\mathbb R^2\). The zero term proves nonnegativity, and substitution gives \(F_h(0,0)=0\). At \((0,1/2)\) the three terms in the original maximum are \(0,-h,-2h\); at \((0,-1/2)\) they are \(0,h,-10h\). This proves the asserted unequal values at opposite points and hence failure of global evenness.

Every lattice point of \(Q_h\), including its boundary, has integer first coordinate between \(-h\) and \(h\) and second coordinate in \(\{-1,0,1\}\). Conversely, every such pair belongs to \(Q_h\). This proves the exact census \(|D_h|=3(2h+1)\). For \(|x|\le h\), direct evaluation on its three rows gives

\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{F_h(x,-1)}{\log 2}
&=\max\{0,|x|+2h,|x|-14h\}=|x|+2h,\\
\frac{F_h(x,0)}{\log 2}
&=\max\{0,|x|,|x|-6h\}=|x|,\\
\frac{F_h(x,1)}{\log 2}
&=\max\{0,|x|-2h,|x|+2h\}=|x|+2h.
\end{aligned}
\]

These evaluations remain valid when \(|x|=h\). Exponentiating proves all stated positive weights. The support and the weight formula are invariant under each coordinate sign change, and every lattice point outside the support remains outside it under those changes. Thus the symmetry holds for the entire table. Pairing \((x,y)\) with \((-x,y)\) cancels its first weighted coordinate, while pairing \((x,y)\) with \((x,-y)\) cancels its second weighted coordinate. The sites fixed by either pairing contribute zero to that coordinate. The finite total is positive because \(w^{(h)}_{(0,0)}=1\), so its normalized mean is exactly zero.

For completeness, define \(f_h:\mathbb R^2\to[0,\infty)\) to equal \(e^{-F_h}\) on \(Q_h\) and zero off \(Q_h\). This is a finite-valued extension of every entry of \(w^{(h)}\), including every table zero. If \(p,p'\in Q_h\) and \(0<\theta<1\), convexity of \(Q_h\) and \(F_h\) gives

\[
f_h((1-\theta)p+\theta p')
=e^{-F_h((1-\theta)p+\theta p')}
\ge e^{-(1-\theta)F_h(p)-\theta F_h(p')}
=f_h(p)^{1-\theta}f_h(p')^\theta.
\]

If either endpoint is outside \(Q_h\), the right side is zero and the same inequality follows from nonnegativity. This verifies exactly the globally extendable complete-table definition in `488f0a583886b5fc`. The shifted objective in the statement samples the globally defined potential \(F_h\); it is not defined by translating this truncated extension \(f_h\).

The elementary finite geometric sum is \(\sum_{x=-h}^{h}2^{-|x|}=1+2\sum_{x=1}^{h}2^{-x}=3-2^{1-h}\). Summing all three original rows therefore yields \(W_h=(3-2^{1-h})(1+2^{1-2h})\). With \(t=2^{-h}\), the condition \(h\ge1\) gives \(0<t\le1/2\), and

\[
W_h-3=(3-2t)(1+2t^2)-3
=-2t(1-t)(1-2t)\le0.
\]

For every real \(L\ge0\), the closed-cutoff sum uses a subset of the complete positive table. Hence \(0<Z_{F_h}(0;L)\le W_h\) and

\[
\frac{Z_{F_h}(0;L)}{1+L}
\le\frac{W_h}{1+L}\le W_h\le3.
\]

This bound holds for every cutoff before maximization. The cost values form the finite set \(\{0,1,\ldots,h,2h,2h+1,\ldots,3h\}\log 2\). Given any \(L\ge0\), replacing it by the largest cost value at most \(L\) leaves the numerator unchanged and weakly decreases the denominator. Such a value exists because zero is a cost. Thus the maximum is attained at a cost value, and the preceding bound proves \(M_h\le W_h\le3\). Only \((0,0)\) has cost zero, so the cutoff \(L=0\) gives \(M_h\ge1\). No fixed-cutoff value has been substituted for the optimized score.

For the fixed shift \(v=(0,-1/2)\), a site \((x,y)\in D_h\) is evaluated at \((x,y+1/2)\). Direct evaluation of every original row, again for all \(|x|\le h\), gives

\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{F_h(x,-1/2)}{\log 2}
&=\max\{0,|x|+h,|x|-10h\}=|x|+h,\\
\frac{F_h(x,1/2)}{\log 2}
&=\max\{0,|x|-h,|x|-2h\}=0,\\
\frac{F_h(x,3/2)}{\log 2}
&=\max\{0,|x|-3h,|x|+6h\}=|x|+6h.
\end{aligned}
\]

The middle-row equality includes both endpoints \(x=\pm h\). The third evaluation is valid even though \(y+1/2=3/2\) lies outside \(Q_h\), since \(F_h\) is defined on all of \(\mathbb R^2\). The middle row contributes exactly \(2h+1\); the lower and upper rows contribute \(2^{-h}(3-2^{1-h})\) and \(2^{-6h}(3-2^{1-h})\), respectively. This proves the complete shifted-sum formula with no lattice site omitted. Its value is at least \(2h+1\). Since \(M_h>0\) and \(4M_h\le12\), it follows that its ratio to \(2^2M_h\) is at least \((2h+1)/12\). The supremum over all real shifts is at least this value at the same fixed \(v\), proving the claimed divergence and the failure of every finite proposed constant.

The only even second coordinate in \(\{-1,0,1\}\) is zero. Thus \(Q_h\cap(2\mathbb Z^2)\) consists exactly of \((2k,0)\) with \(-\lfloor h/2\rfloor\le k\le\lfloor h/2\rfloor\). Every one of these sites has shifted cost zero by the middle-row calculation. Counting them proves the exact parity sum; division by \(M_h\le3\) proves its divergent ratio.

The loss of the global-evenness step in `f0ff12aa81c7461c` can also be seen directly within this parity class. For \(h\ge2\), take \(p=(0,0)\) and \(q=(2,0)\). Both are occupied sites of parity \((0,0)\), and \(F_h(p-v)=F_h(q-v)=0\). Nevertheless \(F_h((q-p)/2)=F_h(1,0)=\log 2>0\). The same-parity difference estimate \(F_h((q-p)/2)\le(F_h(q-v)+F_h(p-v))/2\), justified there by global evenness and convexity, is false here. All original lattice costs remain symmetric and the original mean remains zero, as already verified.
statement:
All logarithms are natural. For every integer \(h\ge1\), set \(s=2\), \(Q_h=[-h,h]\times[-1,1]\), and \(v=(0,-1/2)\). Define the globally finite potential

\[
F_h(x,y)=(\log 2)\max\{0,\ |x|-2hy,\ |x|+8hy-6h\}
\qquad ((x,y)\in\mathbb R^2).
\]

The body \(Q_h\) is origin-symmetric and compact with nonempty interior. The function \(F_h:\mathbb R^2\to[0,\infty)\) is convex and satisfies \(F_h(0,0)=0\), but is not even. Use \(D_h=Q_h\cap\mathbb Z^2\) and the complete lattice table \(w^{(h)}_z=e^{-F_h(z)}\) for \(z\in D_h\), with \(w^{(h)}_z=0\) at every other lattice point. In the complete-table notation of accepted fact `488f0a583886b5fc`, the integer dimension is \(n=s=2\), the positive support \(D\) is \(D_h\), and the total mass \(W\) is \(W_h=\sum_{z\in D_h}w^{(h)}_z\). This table is globally extendable in that fact's sense. Its complete positive support and weights are

\[
\begin{aligned}
D_h&=\{-h,-h+1,\ldots,h\}\times\{-1,0,1\},\\
w^{(h)}_{(x,y)}&=2^{-|x|-2h|y|}\qquad ((x,y)\in D_h).
\end{aligned}
\]

Consequently, for all \((x,y)\in\mathbb Z^2\) and \(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2\in\{-1,1\}\), one has \(w^{(h)}_{(\epsilon_1x,\epsilon_2y)}=w^{(h)}_{(x,y)}\), including all zero entries, and \(W_h^{-1}\sum_{z\in D_h}w^{(h)}_z z=(0,0)\).

Use the exact central-cutoff convention of accepted fact `f0ff12aa81c7461c`, with its \(Q,F,D,M\) respectively equal to \(Q_h,F_h,D_h,M_h\):

\[
Z_{F_h}(0;L)=\sum_{\substack{z\in D_h\\F_h(z)\le L}}e^{-F_h(z)},
\qquad
M_h=\max_{L\ge0}\frac{Z_{F_h}(0;L)}{1+L}.
\]

This maximum is attained and satisfies \(1\le M_h\le W_h\le3\). More precisely, the original total and the complete shifted sum are

\[
\begin{aligned}
W_h&=(3-2^{1-h})(1+2^{1-2h}),\\
\sum_{z\in D_h}e^{-F_h(z-v)}
&=(2h+1)+(2^{-h}+2^{-6h})(3-2^{1-h}).
\end{aligned}
\]

In particular,

\[
\frac{\displaystyle\sup_{u\in\mathbb R^2}
\sum_{z\in D_h}e^{-F_h(z-u)}}{2^2M_h}
\ge\frac{2h+1}{12}\longrightarrow\infty
\qquad (h\longrightarrow\infty).
\]

Thus no finite absolute constant can bound the full shifted mass by \(2^s\) times the optimized central-cutoff score under the proposed replacement hypotheses, even for fixed \(s=2\). The parity class \(c=(0,0)\) alone satisfies

\[
\sum_{z\in Q_h\cap(2\mathbb Z^2)}e^{-F_h(z-v)}
=2\lfloor h/2\rfloor+1,
\qquad
\frac{\displaystyle\sum_{z\in Q_h\cap(2\mathbb Z^2)}e^{-F_h(z-v)}}{M_h}
\ge\frac{2\lfloor h/2\rfloor+1}{3}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]

The exact failed hypothesis is global evenness: \(F_h(0,1/2)=0\) while \(F_h(0,-1/2)=h\log 2>0\).
